title: The Pain of the Shackles
next_chapter_hook: Before Su Qingyao's words finished, Chen Ji saw her fingertips trembling slightly— what had she discovered in the Holy Sect's texts?

text.content: The moment the Tianji Record shuddered violently, Chen Ji felt as if his chest had been struck by thunder. The crack did not come from the external world, but spread from the depths of the runes, like cracked mud on a dried riverbed, inch by inch extending in all directions. Agonizing pain surged into his Mental Sea like a tide. He knelt on one knee, biting his tongue hard, crimson blood droplets sliding down the corner of his lips. The faint light formed by Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul swayed violently, as if enduring something for its host, yet could only emit a sigh: 'The shackles loosen... the price is backlash.'

Chen Ji raised his wrist, his pupils contracting sharply. What was once a faint shackle pattern was now clearly carved, pitch-black lines coiling around his wrist bones like living creatures gently squirming. He could clearly perceive— this was no ordinary mark, but a temporal chain bound to his lifespan. Each time the pattern pulsed, he felt an emptiness in his chest, as if some intangible寿命 was being drawn from his body. Moonlight through the window lattice cast down, making those chain-like patterns glisten with a cold, eerie light.

dialogue.content: 'Young fool, you merely attempted to foresee a trivial matter three breaths ahead, yet cost yourself three months of lifespan.' Mo Xiansheng's voice emerged from the pages, carrying undeniable weight, 'The Tianji Record's shackles were never a prison, but a contract of equivalent exchange. The more significant the命运的 thread you alter, the more severe the backlash.'

text.content: Three months of lifespan, merely to watch a falling leaf's landing spot. Chen Ji laughed softly, that smile more distressing than crying. He lowered his gaze, hiding his wrist within his sleeve, though his fingertips trembled beneath the fabric. Posing as atrash for so many years, he had long grown accustomed to pressing all pain deep within his heart, always wearing that unruffled mask. Yet the current pain was so tangible, as if someone was slowly carving warnings into his五脏六腑, each stroke a warning.

dialogue.content: 'Chen Ji!' The door was violently pushed open, Su Qingyao's figure appearing in the moonlight. She had been conducting her nightly inspection rounds when she noticed unusual light emanating from this servant disciple's room. Rushing to investigate, she stumbled upon this scene. Chen Ji's disheveled appearance— kneeling on the ground, blood at his lips— struck her heart. Despite her usual cold demeanor, she felt as if someone had violently clutched her heart, 'What is this... what's going on?'

text.content: Chen Ji braced himself against the table, rising slowly, deliberately slowing his movements as if to conceal his earlier loss of composure. He raised his hand to wipe away the blood at his lips, subtly turning his face away, unwilling to let Su Qingyao see his pallor: 'The Inner Disciple Senior Fellow visiting my Servant Quarters so late at night— does she have urgent business?' His voice remained indifferent and aloof as always, even carrying hints of his usual sarcasm. Yet the veins on the back of his hand by his side bulged slightly, nails deeply嵌入 his palm— traces of his desperate忍耐 of pain.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao frowned deeply, closing the distance in three quick strides, and without ceremony grabbed his wrist to examine it. The shackle patterns subtly contracted at her touch, as if deliberately hiding something, yet ultimately failing to completely conceal themselves. She sucked in a sharp breath, her voice involuntarily rising: 'What is this? How do you have something like this on you? Who in the entire Tianqing Sect would dare—' 'None of your concern.' Chen Ji interrupted her, his tonecalm得近乎cold, 'Senior Sister Su is well-informed— has she ever seen such a pattern?'

text.content: Su Qingyao did not answer immediately. She released Chen Ji's wrist, stepping back half a pace, her gaze complexly sweeping across his face. This servant disciple— she had been observing him for a long time: from his initial submissive acceptance when bullied by everyone, to the various inexplicable actions she couldn't see through later. Clearly of low cultivation, yet always able to turn danger into safety at critical moments; seemingly of mediocre talent, yet seemingly well-versed in major sect affairs. That vague guess in her heart grew clearer, but seeing the striking bloodstains at the corner of his lips now, she found herself momentarily unable to utter any questioning words.

dialogue.content: 'I once read similar records in Holy Sect remnants.' Su Qingyao finally spoke, her voice low, 'Those were forbidden techniques used to bind prophets in ancient times, trading the practitioner's lifespan for the ability to peer into heavenly secrets. Each time it was used, the shackles tightened one degree, until the host was eventually exhausted to death.' She paused, her gaze burning as she stared at Chen Ji, 'I'm asking you one final time— who exactly are you?'

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao's questioning pointed directly at the core; Chen Ji must make a choice: continue hiding, or reveal part of the truth?

choices.text: Endure to the end, continue the disguise
choices.description: Use histrash persona to dispel her doubts, covering the truth with nonchalant lies. Since the risk of exposure is too great, better to continue playing the wrong role, pushing her back into the position of investigator.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain the existing balance of the relationship
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao's suspicions may deepen, but she temporarily lacks evidence

text.content: Chen Ji pulled at the corner of his lips, revealing a weak yet self-mocking smile: 'Senior Sister Su, if I possessed such abilities, how could I have been idling away in the Servant Quarters all this time? I merely mistakenly consumed an elixir of unknown origin, leaving me with an aftereffect.' He spoke so casually, as if discussing the weather today.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao stared at him for a long while, finally harrumphing and sweeping out. Before leaving, she left behind these words: 'Chen Ji, you think I'm foolish? These shackle patterns are clearly backlash traces from actively using abilities— you can deceive others, but not me.'

choices.description: Acknowledge the existence of the shackles, but conceal the Tianji Record's specific abilities, only claiming someone placed forbidden techniques on him. Utilize Su Qingyao's role as investigator, letting her proactively seek解除 methods for him.
choices.visible_reward: Opportunity to gain Su Qingyao's assistance
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao may investigate deeper, bringing more trouble

text.content: Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, finally letting out a sigh: 'Since Senior Sister Su has already seen through the situation, I won't keep hiding it. Three years ago, I obtained an ancient jade by chance. After wearing it, these shackle patterns appeared on my body. Each time I use... a special ability, my lifespan is diminished.' He spoke half-truths, yet a flicker of subtle sharpness flashed in his eyes.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao heard this, giving him a complex look. That gaze held scrutiny, doubt, but even more of something she herself couldn't explain... heartache. She recalled how he had knelt on the ground, forcefully enduring the pain just now, and her chest tightened again: "Since you knew it would cost you lifespan, why still use that ability?"

text.content: Chen Ji did not answer this question. He turned around, gazing at the cold bright moon beyond the window, his spine straight as if no storm in this world could bend him. But Su Qingyao noticed the hand hidden in his sleeve was trembling slightly, the shackle patterns visibly tightening, like some greedy creature devouring his life. She unconsciously clenched her fist.

dialogue.content: "I will investigate the origin of this shackle." Su Qingyao's voice came from behind him, carrying unwavering resolve. "The Holy Sect's archives are vast as an ocean—there's bound to be a method to解除 the forbidden technique. You... hold on for now." Her tone remained cold and aloof, yet when she reached those last two words, she paused slightly, as if afraid to disturb something.

text.content: Chen Ji heard this, and a very faint arc curved at the corner of his mouth. Not mockery, not self-mockery, but something nearly gentle flickered past. He did not turn around, merely saying softly: "Su Senior Sister, you shouldn't wade into these muddy waters." Though he spoke thus, his mind was already rapidly calculating—if Su Qingyao could truly find a method of relief, he could free up more Heavenly Fate Value for his schemes. This piece was worth investing in.

dialogue.content: "Whether I wade into it or not is my own business." Su Qingyao snorted coldly, but suddenly paused at the doorway. "By the way, I once read in an ancient text about a record—there exists a divine medicine called 'Heavenly Fate Lotus' within the Holy Sect's secret realm. Legend says it can repair broken destinies and release all forbidden restraints. However, that place is extremely dangerous—ordinary people who go there are simply courting death." She did not say more, her figure vanishing into the night.

text.content: Moonlight filtered through the window lattice, stretching Chen Ji's shadow long across the floor. He lowered his head to gaze at the increasingly tight shackle patterns on his wrist, then suddenly let out a low laugh. The Holy Sect's secret realm, Heavenly Fate Lotus... Su Qingyao ah Su Qingyao, do you know that with a single casual remark, you have already fallen into my chess game? After the laugh, pain struck again. He groaned, falling onto the bedside, fine cold sweat soaking his temples. Mo Xiansheng's voice drifted over: "Young one, you're playing with fire."

choice.prompt: After Su Qingyao left, Chen Ji faced the shackle's pain alone. How should he respond?

choices.description: Clench his teeth and weather this wave of backlash, turning the pain into sharpening of will. Since he chose this path, there is no room for retreat.
choices.visible_reward: Willpower strengthens, laying foundation for bearing heavier costs later
choices.risk_hint: If the backlash is too severe, he may lose consciousness, arousing others' suspicion

text.content: Chen Ji sat cross-legged on the bed, hands forming seals, guiding the chaotic qi within his body through breathing techniques. The shackle patterns tightened in waves, bringing soul-tearing agony. He did not utter a sound, merely pressing his lips into a pale straight line. Cold sweat soaked through the back of his robes, yet he seemed utterly oblivious, his gaze calm and deep as an abyss. Mo Xiansheng sighed beside him: "This young one actually possesses some of Chen Xuan's resilience from back then."

choices.text: Study the Tianji Record, searching for alternative methods
choices.description: Since backlash is unavoidable, try to find a method with lesser consumption. Since Mo Xiansheng knows the origins of the Tianji Record, perhaps there are secrets he has yet to reveal.
choices.visible_reward: May discover methods to reduce backlash, or unlock new abilities
choices.risk_hint: The study process may trigger new prohibitions

text.content: Straining to flip through the Tianji Record, Chen Ji's gaze fell upon those obscure, hard-to-decipher symbols. Mo Xiansheng's voice适时响起: "This is the third realm of the Tianji Record—'Borrowing Momentum.' If you can draw the power of heaven and earth to serve yourself, rather than solely propelling it with your own lifespan, the backlash will naturally lessen. However... your current cultivation is far from sufficient." He paused, "Unless you can find someone whose destiny aligns with yours, to share this calamity."

dialogue.content: "Share this calamity?" Chen Ji's brow slightly raised. "The gentleman's meaning is—" "The Art of Shared Life." Mo Xiansheng's voice carried several layers of profound meaning. "In ancient times, a pair ofdao companions used this method to survive a life-and-death ordeal together. However, this technique is extremely dangerous. Once formed, the two are bound by shared fate—if one dies, the other cannot survive alone."

text.content: Chen Ji closed the Tianji Record, his fingertips gently stroking the cover. The Art of Shared Life sounded beautiful, but where in this world is there such a windfall? Moreover, in his chess game, Su Qingyao was a crucial piece. If he made her share life with him, wouldn't that completely bind her to his own fate? This thought merely turned once in his mind before he set it aside. He would not take this step unless absolutely necessary. The night deepened, and the shackle patterns finally stopped tightening. He exhaled a long breath of turbid air, closing his eyes exhaustedly.

dialogue.content: The next morning, Su Qingyao came to the Servants' Quarters again, a yellowed ancient scroll in her hands. Without knocking, she pushed the door open directly. What met her eyes was Chen Ji leaning against the headboard, his wrists wrapped in bandages. Her footsteps faltered momentarily, then she strode forward quickly. Though her tone remained cold, a hint of irrepressible worry hid in the depths of her eyes: "I searched all night—this is a fragment scroll recording the shackle forbidden technique from Holy Sect archives. Look at this first. If there's anything you don't understand, I can explain it for you."

text.content: Chen Ji took the ancient scroll, his gaze sweeping across those yellowed pages. The content recorded was not much different from what Mo Xiansheng had said—the shackle forbidden technique originated from the ancient seer lineage, trading lifespan for the ability to peer into heavenly secrets. The only three methods of解除 were: first, cultivate to great accomplishment, breaking the technique by force; second, find a person of shared destiny to share the ordeal; third, seek the divine medicine Heavenly Fate Lotus to reshape one's fate. He returned the scroll to Su Qingyao, a faint smile curving his lips: "Su Senior Sister has truly been diligent."

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao took the scroll, looking at him with a complicated expression: "None of these three methods are easily achievable. The first requires supreme cultivation, the second requires finding someone willing to die for you, and the third is even more remote... The Holy Sect's secret realm has a fearsome reputation—ordinary people who enter are dead for sure." She paused, her voice lowering: "What do you plan to do?"

choice.prompt: Faced with Su Qingyao's questioning, how does Chen Ji respond?

choices.text: Acting relaxed, not wanting her to worry
choices.description: Using a casual attitude to dismiss her concerns, making Su Qingyao believe he doesn't care about the pain, maintaining his 'waste' persona.
choices.visible_cost: Su Qingyao might think he's beyond saving
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao might become more determined to uncover the truth

dialogue.content: Chen Ji shrugged, appearing indifferent: "Senior Sister Su, no need to worry. This worthless life of mine isn't worth much anyway—each day I survive is a gain. As for Heavenly Fate Lotus, I don't dare hope for such things." His tone was overly light, as if discussing someone else's life and death.

Su Qingyao heard this, her brow furrowed deeply, a flash of anger flickering in her eyes: "Chen Ji, do you think I'm bored enough to come find you?" Her voice suddenly turned cold. "Someone like you, knowingly walking into a deadly trap yet still forcing yourself to hold on, clearly full of secrets yet pretending to care about nothing... What exactly are you afraid of?"

choices.text: Rarely revealing his true feelings, choosing to be honest with her
choices.description: Dropping the mask, showing Su Qingyao his vulnerable side. This is a risky emotional investment, but if successful, it can greatly increase her dependence on him.
choices.visible_reward: Su Qingyao's goodwill and trust increase significantly, possibly unlocking deeper relationship paths
choices.risk_hint: If Su Qingyao turns against him in the future, these sincere words will all become leverage

text.content: Chen Ji remained silent for a long moment, then let out a soft sigh. That sigh seemed to surge from the depths of his soul, carrying years of accumulated weariness and heaviness. He raised his head, meeting Su Qingyao's eyes for the first time. Those eyes no longer held their usual mockery and distance, only a still pool of dead water: "I'm not afraid of anything... It's just that some things, even if spoken, have no meaning. This shackle is a price I must bear, unrelated to anyone else."

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao was stunned. She had never seen Chen Ji like this—that disciple always wearing a grin, full of sarcasm, now appearing like a beast covered in wounds, alone in the darkness licking its wounds. She suddenly felt a sharp ache in her chest, and almost unconsciously reached out, gently placing her hand over his bandaged wrist: "I will help you. Whether you're willing or not, I will help."

choices.memory_label: 苏青瑶决定帮助陈机解除枷锁

text.content: Chen Ji lowered his head, looking at Su Qingyao's hand resting on his wrist, his pupils slightly contracting. That hand was slender and fair, yet the fingertips bore calluses from years of sword work, feeling cool to the touch. He didn't pull his hand back, only saying softly: "Senior Sister Su, we share no kinship—why risk yourself for this waste of a person?" Despite his words, an inexplicable ripple stirred in his heart. How many years had it been since he walked alone on the edge of a blade? Never had anyone spoken to him like this. This woman... could she really be just a coincidence?

dialogue.content: "No kinship?" Su Qingyao snorted coldly, standing up and looking down at him, "When I, Su Qingyao, do things, I only ask my heart, never the reason. I knew long ago that you have secrets. But since you don't say, I won't ask—I only help you solve the troubles before you. As for whether you're willing to tell me the truth in the future, that's a matter for later." She paused, her voice softening slightly, "Rest well and heal. As for the Heavenly Fate Lotus... I'll look to see if there are any other clues."

text.content: Su Qingyao turned and left, her steps still cold and proud, but at the moment she crossed the threshold, she slightly turned her head. Morning light fell upon her profile, outlining a gentle contour. Chen Ji watched her figure disappear at the end of the Corridor, slowly withdrawing his gaze, and lowered his head to look at the shackle patterns on his own wrist. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his Mental Sea: "This little girl is quite interesting... Lad, are you sure you won't tell her about the existence of the Tianji Record?" Chen Ji gave no answer, only tucking his wrist into his sleeve, a meaningful curve appearing at the corner of his lips. Tell Su Qingyao? Not yet. This piece... has just begun to be used.
